stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model belongs to the Llama family, indicating its relevance in the large language model (LLM) space.
The associated pipeline and tags confirm its use for text-generation tasks within the Hugging Face ecosystem.

stories.title: Microsoft confirms Copilot ‘super app’ coming this year
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Microsoft is developing an AI 'super app' centered around Copilot.
This new application will integrate Copilot's chat, coding, and agentic features.
The 'super app' is slated for release this year and will target both consumer and commercial markets.

stories.title: Mark Zuckerberg is planning a big push into personal AI agents
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Meta is heavily investing in AI, signaling a major strategic focus.
The company plans a significant push into personal AI agents capable of autonomous task execution.
Mark Zuckerberg previewed this high-level vision during the Q2 2026 earnings call.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a generative AI.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the current LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a substantial developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance using Gemma 4 saw up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes local-first operation, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating with local LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance gains.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing local AI inference.
This is available in preview, signaling a major step toward optimized on-device AI experiences.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, ensuring data processing occurs entirely on the user's device.
The core value proposition is providing private, on-device AI assistance for coding tasks.

stories.title: Xbox revenue drops 10 percent as Microsoft’s cloud and AI business surges
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Xbox revenue saw a 10% dip, driven by declines in content and services like Game Pass.
Xbox hardware sales experienced a 13% decline in the reported quarter.
This downturn is contrasted by a surge in Microsoft's overall cloud and AI business.

stories.title: Mythos attack on 3rd-round PQC algorithm candidate puts it out of commission
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A significant vulnerability was discovered in the HAWK algorithm, a candidate for Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC).
The weakness was found through an attack methodology named 'Mythos', indicating a major cryptographic breakthrough in cryptanalysis.
This discovery effectively removes HAWK from contention in the ongoing standardization process for quantum-resistant encryption.

stories.title: Anthropic is finding bugs faster than Microsoft can fix them
stories.author: Renee Dudley, ProPublica
bullet_points: Anthropic is reportedly discovering security vulnerabilities in its models at a faster rate than Microsoft can patch them.
The news highlights a significant and ongoing security challenge within the rapidly evolving AI landscape.
Microsoft is reportedly engaged in an urgent, behind-the-scenes effort to address these emerging exploits.

stories.title: Can AI agents conduct open-ended AI research? Early evidence from two case studies
stories.author: Arvind Narayanan
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical, yet unproven, concept of AI agents conducting open-ended AI research.
It critiques existing evaluation methods, noting that current tests are either too narrow or rely on unreliable peer review.
The authors propose a novel third methodology to measure progress toward automating AI Research and Development (R&D).

stories.title: APEX-Accounting
stories.author: Bertie Vidgen
bullet_points: Introduction of APEX-Accounting, a new benchmark designed to test frontier AI models on real-world accounting tasks.
The benchmark covers core accounting functions such as account reconciliation, expense accrual, transaction posting, and report generation.
The private evaluation set features 160 expert-authored tasks across 10 simulated accounting worlds, incorporating various file types (spreadsheets, PDFs).

stories.title: Can AI agents conduct open-ended AI research? Early evidence from two case studies
stories.author: Arvind Narayanan
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical, yet unproven, concept of AI agents conducting open-ended AI research.
It critiques existing evaluation methods, noting they are either too narrow or rely on unreliable peer review processes.
The authors propose a novel third methodology to measure progress toward automating AI Research & Development (R&D).

stories.title: MindForge: Teaching Small Language Models Whole-Life-Cycle Software Engineering via Source-Free Program Synthesis
stories.author: Ahmed E. Hassan
bullet_points: Introduces 'MindForge,' a new method to teach small language models complete software engineering lifecycles.
Addresses the critical challenge of 'from-scratch' program synthesis, where current frontier models perform poorly (under 1% on ProgramBench).
Overcomes the limitation of lacking scalable training environments that cover the entire software development process.

stories.title: APEX-Accounting
stories.author: Bertie Vidgen
bullet_points: Introduction of APEX-Accounting, a new benchmark designed to test frontier models' capability in real-world accounting tasks.
The benchmark, developed by Mercor and Ramp, covers complex tasks like account reconciliation, expense accrual, and report generation.
The evaluation uses a private set of 160 tasks across 10 simulated 'worlds,' authored and solved by accounting experts.

stories.title: DenseOn with the LateOn: Fully Open Dense and Late-Interaction Models for Multilingual, Long-Context, and Code Search
stories.author: Amélie Chatelain
bullet_points: Introduces DenseOn with LateOn, a fully open model for multilingual, long-context, and code search.
Addresses the reproducibility gap in state-of-the-art retrieval models by providing an open training recipe.
Utilizes a large-scale dataset (665M English pairs from 34 public sources) and translate-train for multilingual transfer.

stories.title: On-Policy Distillation for LLM Safety: A Routing Approach to Template-Robust Realignment
stories.author: Sheng Wen
bullet_points: Addresses a critical vulnerability in LLM fine-tuning where malicious data can embed harmful behaviors.
Proposes an 'On-Policy Distillation' routing approach to enhance LLM safety and alignment.
Overcomes limitations of existing safety defenses, such as catastrophic forgetting and reduced effectiveness.

stories.title: Slopsquatting: The Supply Chain Attack That Weaponizes AI Hallucinations
stories.author: nazar-boyko
bullet_points: Introduces 'Slopsquatting,' a novel supply chain attack vector targeting AI systems.
This attack specifically exploits the tendency of AI models to 'hallucinate' or generate incorrect information.
It is framed as an evolution of traditional typosquatting, weaponizing AI assistant vulnerabilities.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically benefiting users on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The new feature set includes the capability for web search functionality in Claude Code.
This update enhances the complexity and capability of AI agents running through Ollama.

stories.title: Qualcomm is raising phone chip prices starting September 1st
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Qualcomm is implementing price increases across its range of phone processors.
The price hikes are scheduled to take effect starting September 1st.
The announcement was made by Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon.

stories.title: xAI’s last-minute scramble to stop Minnesota’s anti-nudification app law
stories.author: Sarah Jeong
bullet_points: xAI is challenging a Minnesota law targeting 'nudification' apps through a lawsuit.
The company claims the law's punitive measures force them to restrict Grok Imagine's image-editing features.
The core legal argument presented by xAI is that the state statute violates the First Amendment.

stories.title: Musk went to “war,” sought jail time for X ad boycotts—but case ends with a whimper
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Musk pursued legal action against advertisers boycotting X.
The legal battle regarding the ad boycotts concluded without a major ruling.
Advertisers ultimately agreed to re-establish their relationship with X.

stories.title: Who wins and who loses after US bans foreign robots?
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: The article discusses the potential negative impact of a US government ban on foreign-made robots.
The core argument suggests the ban might impede rather than advance US domestic robotics development.
This touches upon geopolitical trade policy intersecting with advanced automation technology.

stories.title: Elon Musk’s xAI is trying to sue its way out of a Grok reckoning
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: xAI, Elon Musk's AI venture, is reportedly engaging in legal action regarding Grok.
Musk is defending Grok against a ban enacted by Minnesota.
The core legal argument centers on the claim that the app ban is unconstitutional.

stories.title: The Social Cost of an AI Teammate: How an Artificial Teammate Reshapes Human-Human Communication in Small-Team Decision-Making
stories.author: Spencer JaQuay
bullet_points: Investigates the sociocognitive impact of integrating conversational AI as a teammate in small-team decision-making.
Uses a randomized controlled study involving moral-dilemma tasks to analyze communication dynamics.
Examines how the presence of an AI teammate reshapes human-human interaction within a team setting.

stories.title: Improving Item Discoverability in e-Commerce Search via Related Intent Generation
stories.author: Tejaswi Tenneti
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in traditional e-commerce search by prioritizing discoverability over strict query matching.
Proposes a scalable system using 'intent-conditioned recall expansion' to find related items.
Focuses on improving user satisfaction and commercial outcomes, particularly in grocery retail.

stories.title: OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Office-Suite Tasks with Economic Grounding
stories.author: Hua Wu
bullet_points: Introduces OmegaUse-OfficeVal, a new benchmark for evaluating LLM agents.
The benchmark specifically tests agents on long-horizon office-suite tasks.
A key feature is the inclusion of task-level economic grounding to assess cost-effectiveness.

stories.title: Cost-Sensitive Conformal Prediction and Human-in-the-Loop Abstention for Imbalanced High-Stakes Decision Support: A Multi-Domain Benchmark
stories.author: Shyamal Lakhanpal
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in standard Conformal Prediction (CP) when applied to high-stakes, imbalanced datasets.
Demonstrates that standard CP severely under-covers rare, costly minority classes (e.g., fraud, rare diseases).
Proposes Cost-Sensitive CP and Human-in-the-Loop Abstention as solutions for reliable uncertainty quantification in critical domains.

stories.title: Linguistic Monoculture in LLM-Assisted Language Use
stories.author: Lutz Oettershagen
bullet_points: Widespread reliance on LLMs for text generation and revision may lead to 'linguistic monoculture'.
This phenomenon suggests that shared LLM models could reduce natural variation in population-level language use.
The research proposes a mathematical framework to model the interaction between authors and LLMs as distributions over linguistic features.

stories.title: Do You Really Need to Pretrain Q-Functions for Online RL Fine-Tuning?
stories.author: Chelsea Fin
bullet_points: Challenges the conventional wisdom in Reinforcement Learning (RL) regarding the necessity of pre-training Q-functions.
Presents evidence that online RL can achieve high performance and reliability even with a randomly initialized Q-function.
Suggests a potential simplification or shift in the standard 'pretrain-then-fine-tune' paradigm for value-based RL.

stories.title: Skillful forecasting of offshore winds from satellite scatterometer constellations
stories.author: Angela Meyer
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical need for accurate, short-term (minutes to hours) forecasts of offshore winds for power system stability.
Traditional Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) models are not optimized for the short lead times where initial-condition accuracy is paramount.
The study proposes using satellite scatterometer observations directly for forecasting, moving beyond their current assimilation role in NWP.

stories.title: Cost-Sensitive Conformal Prediction and Human-in-the-Loop Abstention for Imbalanced High-Stakes Decision Support: A Multi-Domain Benchmark
stories.author: Shyamal Lakhanpal
bullet_points: Addresses a critical flaw in standard Conformal Prediction (CP) when applied to high-stakes, imbalanced datasets.
Demonstrates that standard CP severely under-covers rare, costly minority classes (e.g., fraud, critical medical events).
Proposes a solution involving Cost-Sensitive CP and Human-in-the-Loop Abstention for robust uncertainty quantification.

stories.title: Mental World Modeling
stories.author: Yiran Zhao
bullet_points: The paper addresses the limitation of current world models, which only predict physical states (what/where things are).
It argues that human behavior is driven by hidden mental states (beliefs, intentions, desires) that physical models ignore.
The core contribution is the formulation of Mental World Modeling (MWM) to incorporate agent knowledge and beliefs into predictive systems.

stories.title: SpecFirst: Behavioral Specification Elicitation as a First-Class Step in Agent-Based Program Synthesis from Scratch
stories.author: Ahmed E. Hassan
bullet_points: Program synthesis from scratch remains a major challenge for LLM-based agents, even with advanced models.
Current benchmarks (e.g., ProgramBench) show frontier models struggle significantly when only given natural language and an execution oracle.
The paper proposes 'SpecFirst,' which treats behavioral specification elicitation as a distinct, crucial step in the synthesis process.

stories.title: OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Office-Suite Tasks with Economic Grounding
stories.author: Hua Wu
bullet_points: Introduces OmegaUse-OfficeVal, a new benchmark for evaluating LLM agents.
Focuses on long-horizon office-suite tasks, moving beyond simple single-step prompts.
Adds 'economic grounding' to the evaluation, assessing agent performance relative to cost.

stories.title: MindForge: Teaching Small Language Models Whole-Life-Cycle Software Engineering via Source-Free Program Synthesis
stories.author: Ahmed E. Hassan
bullet_points: The research addresses the major challenge of generating complete software programs from scratch, a task where current frontier models perform poorly (under 1% success on ProgramBench).
MindForge proposes a method to teach small language models the entire software engineering lifecycle without requiring access to the original source code (source-free synthesis).
The work aims to overcome the current limitation of lacking scalable training environments for end-to-end software engineering tasks.

stories.title: Linguistic Monoculture in LLM-Assisted Language Use
stories.author: Lutz Oettershagen
bullet_points: Widespread reliance on LLMs for text generation and revision may lead to 'linguistic monoculture'.
This phenomenon suggests that shared LLM outputs could reduce natural variation in human language use.
The research proposes a mathematical framework to model the interaction between authors and LLMs as distributions over linguistic features.

stories.title: Data, Context & RAG Lineage Governance for Enterprise AI Agents
stories.author: jitu028
bullet_points: Focuses on advanced governance for Enterprise AI Agents utilizing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
Details technical implementations such as query-time Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) and cryptographic lineage.
Addresses critical security concerns like outbound payload sanitization within agentic workflows.
